context.implementation_summary: Implemented REQ-200 strictly per the approved design (lib/letflow/design/req200-instance-timeline-rendering.md), passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR. lib/letflow/instances.ex: added resolve_actor_display_name/3 (total 4-level actor fallback: users.display_name lookup -> metadata token_description -> metadata actor_label -> literal "system"), render_description/3 (one clause per the 7 real event types -- INSTANCE_STARTED, TASK_COMPLETED, INSTANCE_CANCELLED, INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND, SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED, EXECUTION_ERROR, TIMER_FIRED -- plus a mandatory trailing generic-fallback clause for any other event_type string), fetch_display_names_by_actor_id/2 (one batched, prefix-scoped Repo query per page over the page's distinct non-nil actor_ids, zero queries when none), and rewrote timeline_item/1 into timeline_item/2 (renames sequence_number->sequence_num and created_at->timestamp, adds actor_display_name and description). timeline/3's body now runs the batch lookup once before mapping the page. lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex: timeline_item_map/1 updated in lockstep (output keys "sequence_num"/"timestamp" plus new passthrough "actor_display_name"/"description"). history_item_map/1, the route/auth macro lines, and lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex were not touched; no file under web/ was added or modified (confirmed by git diff --stat).
context.security_attention_flag: This touches user display_name resolution across a tenant boundary indirectly, via the new batched actor lookup (fetch_display_names_by_actor_id/2). Please specifically verify: (1) the lookup query is prefix-scoped to the SAME tenant schema as the timeline's own instance/event query (it is -- both use the `prefix` threaded through timeline/3's opts, and `users` is itself a per-tenant-schema table per Decision 0006 D1, so the query cannot resolve or leak another tenant's user rows even if a cross-tenant actor_id were ever presented); (2) a deleted user's or the platform sentinel's (00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002, TIMER_FIRED's actor) unresolvable actor_id never errors or leaks anything -- it simply falls through the 4-level fallback chain to metadata or the literal "system", never raising and never returning null/blank; (3) no actor_id, token_description, or actor_label value is ever echoed across a tenant boundary since all three come from either the calling tenant's own users table or that same tenant's own event metadata already scoped by the unchanged instance-existence/ownership check (ensure_instance_exists/2, REQ-072 unchanged).

result.summary: PASS -- no BLOCKER on any applicable invariant. Independently re-ran mix compile (clean), mix format --check-formatted (clean), mix test test/letflow/routers/instances_test.exs (40/40 passing), mix letflow.lint_handoffs (0 new violations), and git diff main...HEAD --stat (scope exactly lib/letflow/instances.ex, lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex, test/letflow/routers/instances_test.exs, the design doc, and handoff/registry/status-index bookkeeping -- no migration, no web/, lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex untouched). Traced fetch_display_names_by_actor_id/2's cross-tenant risk concretely: Letflow.Identity.User is per-tenant-schema (Decision 0006 D1, no tenant_id column per D2), the new query passes the same prefix timeline/3 already threads through its existing event query and ensure_instance_exists/2 (REQ-072, unchanged) -- schema-scoped by construction, cannot resolve another tenant's row even under an adversarial UUID-collision assumption. token_description/actor_label are not set by any writer today (grep confirms) and even if populated would only ever render as escaped JSX text in the SPA (TimelineFeedItem.tsx), never dangerouslySetInnerHTML -- no injection vector. render_description/3's 7 clauses interpolate only already-tenant-scoped actor/payload data, no new query. The generic fallback for open-ended Lua-emitted event_type strings is plain string interpolation into a JSON field rendered as escaped text back to the same authoring tenant only -- no injection vector, no cross-tenant exposure. INV-1 APPLIES and PASSES (prefix-scoped, traced above); INV-2/INV-3/INV-5 NOT-APPLICABLE (pre-S4/S5 per invariants doc's own gating, though REQ-072's 404 path was re-confirmed unchanged as extra diligence); INV-4 APPLIES, satisfied by absence (no secret-resolution code touched, both prescribed greps zero hits); INV-6 discharged by this report; INV-7 APPLIES, satisfied (pure Ecto.Query composition, zero Repo.query/raw-SQL hits); INV-8 APPLIES, satisfied (resolve_actor_display_name/3 and render_description/3 are both total functions with explicit catch-all clauses, no new bare {:ok, x} = pattern).
